name: Wolters Kluwer N.V.
executive_summary: Wolters Kluwer N.V. (WKL.AS) screens as a buy on quantitative value metrics (15/22 models; P/E 11.1, FCF yield 7.1%, dividend yield 4.2%) after a sharp share-price de-rating that news coverage puts at roughly 45–57% over the past year. Primary filing data show a high-quality compounder: 6% organic revenue growth, 83% recurring revenues, adjusted operating margin of 27.5%, ROIC of 18.0%, and adjusted free cash flow of €1,348 million in FY2025. The central debate is whether generative AI is a structural threat to professional information/software peers or a catalyst for Wolters Kluwer’s domain-specific Expert AI platforms—and why the market has repriced the stock so aggressively despite resilient fundamentals. Capital returns remain strong (€2.52 proposed dividend, €500 million 2026 buyback authorisation), but net debt has risen to €4,024 million (2.0× EBITDA) following €871 million of acquisitions, compressing reported equity to €798 million.
investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen flags Wolters Kluwer across five factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with a persistent buy signal (composite 67%, conviction 68%, 4 weeks stable). That profile fits a value investor seeking earnings power at a depressed multiple rather than a deep cyclical or distressed asset.

Business quality aligns with the screen’s quality and moat passes. FY2025 benchmark figures (2025 Full-Year Report, 25 February 2026) show 6% organic revenue growth to €6,125 million, 7% organic growth in recurring revenues (83% of total), and cloud software up 15% organically. Adjusted operating profit rose 9% in constant currencies to €1,687 million; margin expanded 40 basis points to 27.5%. Diluted adjusted EPS grew 9% in constant currencies to €5.29; adjusted FCF grew 10% to €1,348 million. ROIC held at 18.0%. Tax & Accounting (7% organic growth, 35.2% margin) and Health (5% organic, margin to 32.1%) anchor the portfolio.

The valuation hook is the gap between operating performance and market sentiment. At a screen P/E of 11.1 and FCF yield of 7.1%, the market appears to price material AI disruption or growth deceleration that FY2025 results do not yet corroborate. Management guides to continued organic growth, further margin expansion (~28.0%), and high single-digit diluted adjusted EPS growth in 2026, while stepping up product development to 12–13% of revenues for AI. Progressive dividend policy (proposed €2.52, +8%) and ongoing buybacks (€1.1 billion in 2025; up to €500 million in 2026) support total return. For a value investor, the case is buying a recurring-revenue software/information compounder at a cyclically depressed multiple, with capital allocation discipline and an identifiable AI product roadmap—not a speculative turnaround.
financial_review:
Primary source: 2025 Full-Year Report (annual; 25 February 2026). No interim, half-year, or trading-update filing bodies are present in `filings_index.json` (interim count: 0). Q1 2026 trading update is referenced in news (6 May 2026) but is not indexed here; interim trend analysis from primary filings is therefore unavailable.

Revenue and profitability (benchmark figures, filing body)

IFRS reported results (same filing): operating profit €1,735 million (+20%), including a €232 million gain on divestment of the Finance, Risk & Regulatory Reporting (FRR) unit; profit for the period €1,308 million (+21%); diluted EPS €5.64 (+25%). Reported figures are elevated by the FRR disposal; benchmark metrics better reflect underlying run-rate.

Cash flow and capital allocation

- Net cash from operating activities: €1,668 million (FY2024: €1,654 million).
- Capital expenditure: €303 million (5.0% of revenues); cash conversion ratio 103%.
- Dividends paid: €563 million; share repurchases: €1.1 billion (8.6 million shares at average €128.45).
- Acquisition spending, net of cash acquired: €871 million (RASi €386m, Brightflag €436m, Libra up to €90m).
- FRR divestment net proceeds: €399 million.

Balance sheet and leverage (condensed statement of financial position, filing body)

- Total assets: €9,584 million; total equity: €798 million (down from €1,545 million), reflecting buybacks and FX translation losses in OCI (€445 million exchange difference on foreign operations).
- Goodwill: €4,787 million; other intangibles: €1,825 million—tangible book value is deeply negative (Yahoo balance sheet: -€5,814 million at 2025; consistent with filing structure).
- Gross debt: €4,972 million (including two €500 million Eurobonds issued in 2025); net debt: €4,024 million (FY2024: €3,134 million).
- Net-debt-to-EBITDA: 2.0× (FY2024: 1.6×), within stated target range of 1.5–2.5×.
- €600 million revolving credit facility: undrawn at year-end.
- Non-current employee benefits (pension): €62 million.

Divisional highlights

- Tax & Accounting: revenues €1,660m (+7% organic); adjusted margin 35.2% (+200bp).
- Health: revenues €1,596m (+5% organic); margin 32.1%.
- Financial & Corporate Compliance: +3% organic; CTA enforcement suspension reduced BOI reporting revenues.
- Legal & Regulatory: +5% organic; prior-year €15 million pension gain absent.
- Corporate Performance & ESG: +7% organic but adjusted OP margin fell to 7.5% (from 10.2%) on licence mix and third-party implementation costs.

2026 guidance (filing): adjusted OP margin ~28.0%; adjusted FCF €1,300–1,350 million; ROIC 18–19%; high single-digit diluted adjusted EPS growth in constant currencies; product development 12–13% of revenues.

Yahoo fallback (used only where filing bodies provide multi-year context): `financials_annual.json` corroborates IFRS revenue €6,125m, net income €1,308m, diluted EPS €5.64, and operating cash flow €1,668m for 2025, consistent with the annual report. No material discrepancies noted.

Data gap: no indexed interim filing bodies for H1 2025 or Q1/Q3 2026 trading updates; half-year margin, seasonality, and intra-year leverage cannot be verified from primary extracts in this pack.
risks_and_flags:
AI disruption and sentiment. News and peer commentary (e.g. RELX growth vs. AI concerns, 23 July 2026) frame sector anxiety that likely explains the share-price collapse despite solid FY2025 results. Management is accelerating AI spend (12–13% of revenues in 2026) while targeting further margin expansion—a execution risk if returns lag investment.

Leverage and capital intensity. Net debt rose €890 million to €4,024 million; net-debt/EBITDA 2.0×. FY2025 included €871 million of acquisitions plus €1.1 billion of buybacks, funded partly by €1.0 billion of new Eurobond issuance. Management states leverage may temporarily deviate from 1.5–2.5× but expects to return within range; further M&A could dilute margins and ROIC near term (explicit in outlook).

Intangibles and equity base. Goodwill and intangibles total €6,612 million (69% of assets). Reported equity of €798 million is thin; screen ROE of 1.1% reflects this accounting structure, not underlying cash ROIC (18.0% per filing).

Regulatory and cyclical exposures. Suspension of Corporate Transparency Act enforcement (March 2025) reduced beneficial-ownership reporting revenues in Financial & Corporate Compliance. Transactional lending volumes remained subdued. Print decline continues (-4% organic), though impact is modest (~50bp drag on group organic growth).

Pension. Non-current employee benefits €62 million; remeasurement gain €4 million in OCI (FY2025). Legal & Regulatory margin comparison affected by absence of €15 million pension gain in 2024—pension items are manageable but worth monitoring.

Governance and incentives. CEO transition: Nancy McKinstry (retiring) to Stacey Caywood (designated CEO). LTIP 2023–25 vested with TSR ranking 15th of 15 peers—zero TSR payout—highlighting shareholder return underperformance versus compensation peers.

Acquisition integration. €574 million goodwill on 2025 acquisitions; fair values provisional. Contingent consideration on Libra: fair value €47 million.

Filing language. No going-concern qualification. Forward-looking statements cite general economic, FX, M&A, and liquidity risks. Climate-related impairment estimates judged not material. €600 million undrawn RCF and stated liquidity support ongoing operations; covenant detail is not in the condensed extracts.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is voluminous but repetitive—predominantly valuation/debate articles rather than hard news. Material themes:

Strategy and AI (2026): “Wolters Kluwer (ENXTAM:WKL) Launches New AI Tools Across Tax And Compliance” (1 July 2026); “Wolters Kluwer Deepens OpenAI Partnership As Shares Come Under Pressure” (4 June 2026); “Wolters Kluwer Expands Expert AI Tools Across Legal Tax And Compliance” (9 June 2026); Expert AI rollouts in UpToDate, CCH Axcess, Medi-Span, and legal workflows.

Management and leadership: “Is Wolters Kluwer (ENXTAM:WKL) Recasting Its AI Strategy With Tejas Shah’s Appointment?” (3 February 2026); designated CEO Stacey Caywood referenced in FY2025 results release.

M&A: FY2025 acquisitions of RASi, Brightflag, and Libra; FRR divestment to Regnology (December 2025); StandardFusion acquisition (January 2026, post year-end).

Capital returns: “Wolters Kluwer N.V. Proposes Final Dividend for the Financial Year Ended December 31, 2025” (25 February 2026); “Wolters Kluwer Advances 2026 Share Buyback With New €6.6 Million Tranche” (24 July 2026).

Share-price narrative: multiple articles on ~45–57% one-year declines and whether the stock screens as undervalued—e.g. “Has Wolters Kluwer (ENXTAM:WKL) Fallen Too Far To Look Reasonable?” (24 July 2026); “Wolters Kluwer (ENXTAM:WKL) Stock Still Looks Like A Bargain Despite A 57% Slump” (1 July 2026).

Contract wins: “Wolters Kluwer (ENXTAM:WKL) Renews Norway Deal As CCH Tagetik Tops Rankings Again” (24 July 2026).

Competitive context: “RELX's growth accelerates in scientific and legal units” (23 July 2026)—peer resilience may sharpen AI-disruption debate for Wolters Kluwer.

Thin areas: limited indexed primary coverage of pension, covenant, or going-concern topics in news; no major regulatory enforcement headlines in the manifest.
research_rationale: FY2025 primary filings confirm resilient growth, margins, FCF, and capital returns that support the quantitative buy signal, but the absence of indexed interim filings, elevated leverage/intangibles, and unresolved AI-sentiment overhang warrant accumulation rather than full conviction until half-year evidence and 2026 AI investment returns are visible.
